name: Rapamycin

lead: Rapamycin (sirolimus) is a macrolide originally found in a soil bacterium from Easter Island. It is a prescription immunosuppressant used in transplantation and certain rare diseases.

It is the best-replicated lifespan-extending drug in mice, which has driven off-label interest in humans. Human anti-aging benefit is unproven, and a systematic review of human data found limited evidence.

paras: Rapamycin inhibits mTORC1 (and with chronic use, to some extent mTORC2), a nutrient-sensing growth pathway, which promotes autophagy and reduces protein synthesis and cell growth signaling.

Prescription-only. Known adverse effects include mouth ulcers, impaired wound healing, elevated lipids, glucose intolerance and increased infection risk, particularly at transplant doses. Off-label use for longevity is unapproved and should be supervised by a physician.
